thread:
Priya G: Compliance just emailed: they want verifiable import proofs for BYOK HSM imports. Specifically: operator binding, tamper-evident timestamps, and long retention (7 years). Anyone solved this cleanly?
Liam S: We have HSM attestation blobs at import time. Those are signed by the HSM vendor key. The missing piece is a service-side, customer-verifiable timeline that ties operator identity to the attestation.
Jules M: Two constraints: 1) For private/on-prem customers we cannot exfiltrate key material. 2) Customers require the ability to independently verify import records without trusting our internal DB.
Raj (oncall): For runbooks we also need an artifact customers can pull during incident response. Right now we surface audit logs but not a single signed envelope.
Priya G: Proposal sketch: create a signed "import-proof" envelope that contains: operator_principal, operator_session_id, hsm_attestation_blob, import_hash, import_ts, and a signature by a signing key. Store envelope in WORM-enabled objectstore and give customer read access to their envelopes.
Liam S: Who controls the signing key? If it's a Redwood service key customers may push back. Options: (a) sign with our key but provide a verifiable Merkle anchor we publish externally; (b) let HSM sign a secondary attestation if the device supports it; (c) allow customer-managed signing (they pass a verification pubkey we include in envelope).
Jules M: (c) is ideal for customers who want max assurance. For others we can do (a) + publish periodic Merkle roots to a public ledger (or a customer-provided ledger endpoint). That way customers can verify inclusion without moving key material off-network.
sec-bot: Dependency check: audit-uploader uses checksum-v1 (CVE-2022-XXXX) flagged low severity. Patch required before shipping new envelope pipeline.
Priya G: Noted, security patching is a prereq. Also compliance asked for immutable operator binding. We need operator identities anchored to short-lived certs + 2FA and logged session context.
Liam S: Recommend: require OIDC sessions with token binding and mTLS for the import API. Operator_session_id should be an auditable artifact containing the cert thumbprint.
Jules M: Envelope format example (sketch):
```
op: IMPORT
customer_id: cust-42
operator: priya.g@redwood
operator_session: sid-abc123 (cert_thumb: ab:cd:..)
hsm_attestation: base64(...)
import_hash: sha256:...
import_ts: 2025-02-03T12:05:01Z
signature: base64(...)
```
Priya G: Storage: put envelope under s3://redwood-audit/byok/{customer}/{ts}. Enable object lock/legal_hold and replication for Dedicated/Hosted. For Private, provide an operator playbook and automation to enable equivalent WORM settings.
Raj (oncall): Runbook additions: on import failure or signature mismatch, auto-create incident, attach envelope export, and notify sec + customer-security contact. Add steps to verify HSM attestation chain.
Liam S: For cross-region/CSP proofing: compute a daily Merkle tree of all envelopes for a customer and optionally publish the root to a replicated read-only ledger (could be a small Dynamo stream or customer-managed endpoint). Customers can then compare root -> envelope inclusion.
Jules M: Legal/Retention: compliance wants 7 years retention. Our objectstore supports retention policies and WORM on Hosted/Dedicated. Private customers will need instructions and a script to set retention. We must never store raw key material in any envelope. Only hashes/attestations/metadata.
sec-bot: Note: threat model item 4: attacker forging operator_id. Mitigation: require ephemeral operator certs tied to identity provider and include cert thumbprint in envelope. Also rotate service-signing key and publish its public key for verification.
Priya G: Action items: 1) Jules to draft envelope schema + example verification steps (due Tue). 2) Raj to update incident runbook and add verification checklist. 3) Liam to design Merkle anchoring and optional ledger publish. 4) Sec to remediate checksum CVE in audit-uploader.
Liam S: On the signing key question: implement key hierarchy. Use an HSM-backed signing key for envelopes (KMS-backed in Hosted/Dedicated). Publish the public key and rotate per policy. For customers who demand it, provide an API to accept a customer verification pubkey to be included in the envelope metadata.
Jules M: Edge case: imports performed by automation (CI) vs interactive ops. For automation, operator should be a machine principal with a rotation window and an operator owner listed. Include automation-run id and link to CI logs.
Raj (oncall): Verification checklist for runbook (short): 1) Fetch envelope, 2) verify envelope signature against published pubkey, 3) verify HSM attestation signature, 4) check objectstore retention flags (WORM/legal_hold), 5) cross-check operator session logs and cert thumbprint.
Priya G: Good. Compliance also asked for sample customer-facing verification docs. I'll draft a short guide showing verification commands (openssl verify / merkle inclusion) and hand it to them.
Liam S: I'll prototype an envelope generator + storage hook and a small verifier tool (cli) that customers can run against a provided pubkey + or ledger root. ETA: prototype by next Friday.
sec-bot: CI: unit tests for audit-uploader patch running (job #1432).
Jules M: Filing follow-up ticket INFRA-1210 for implementation work and INFSEC-670 for the CVE remediation.
Priya G: Thanks everyone. If we get the prototype and runbook updates, compliance can do a tabletop next month. Closing thread for now.
